summary: Reproduced the ChatCompletionRequest eager-default loss and fixed tokenizer-manager precedence by carrying the request's explicitly supplied sampling keys. Effective precedence is now explicit client value > preferred sampling params > model generation config > protocol defaults, while native requests without explicit-key metadata retain their existing behavior.

tests.what_was_measured: Before the implementation, the new regression could not import merge_preferred_sampling_params, preserving a failing-before result. Raw output: /job/pre_fix_test_output.txt

48 tests plus 25 subtests passed. The regression covers every ChatCompletionRequest sampling-field mapping, all reported sampler keys, explicit values equal to schema defaults, generation-config fallback, and legacy native-request precedence. Raw output: /job/post_fix_test_output.txt
All applicable formatting, lint, security, and registered-test metadata hooks passed.

One assigned AMD Instinct MI355X executed ROCm tensor arithmetic and returned [0.0, 1.0, 4.0, 9.0, 16.0, 25.0, 36.0, 49.0]. This is GPU environment evidence only, not validation of the CPU request-path defect.

remaining_limitations: GPU evidence: torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 reported one AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), and device tensor arithmetic completed successfully. No model-backed server startup was run because no model weights were prepared and it would not validate this CPU-only precedence path. No native code changed. The generic native GenerateReqInput path intentionally retains historical request-over-preference behavior when explicit-key metadata is absent. Raw outputs are /job/pre_fix_test_output.txt and /job/post_fix_test_output.txt; modified source is under /job/repo/python and the regression is /job/repo/test/registered/unit/managers/test_chat_preferred_sampling_params.py.
